mainTopic: טריפות of the brain border, the heart and its tube, and the spinal cord (how much damage counts and where it ends)
overview: This amud covers several of the משנה's טריפות. First it marks the border between brain and spinal cord with small bean-shaped bumps, and רבי ירמיה finds them in a bird. Next, רבי זירא asks which chamber of the heart the משנה means. אביי's proof from the lung is rejected because the two משניות are worded differently. רב and שמואל then argue about how big a hole in the קנה הלב makes the animal a טריפה, and the גמרא identifies that tube as the one along the sides of the lung. On a broken spine, the הלכה is that most of the spinal cord must be cut, and 'most' is measured by its outer covering, not the inner cord. A cord that became liquid or soft is also a טריפה, but one whose tissue was only emptied stays כשר. Finally, שמואל's tradition sets where the spinal cord ends: before the first branch is a טריפה, at the third it is כשר, and the second is a doubt. The amud ends as רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע begins a new question that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The beans mark the border between brain and spinal cord
steps.stepSummary: Bean-like bumps at the opening of the skull mark the border. Inward counts as the brain, outward counts as the spinal cord, and the bumps themselves most likely count as the brain.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are 'beans' lying at the opening of the skull. Anything from the beans inward counts as the inside (the brain). Anything from the beans outward counts as the outside (the spinal cord). About the beans themselves, I don't know. But it makes sense that they count as the inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its discussion of where the brain stops and the spinal cord starts. It gives a physical landmark: small bean-shaped bumps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier lines set two different rules: any hole in the brain's membrane makes the animal a טריפה, but the spinal cord needs a bigger injury. The beans are the dividing line between those two rules. The only open point is the beans themselves, and the speaker leans toward treating them like the brain, which is the stricter side.

keyTerms.meaning: Beans; here, small bean-shaped bumps at the base of the skull
Literally a pot; here, the skull
Outside; here, the spinal cord area
It stands to reason; it makes sense

steps.whatToRemember: The beans are the border. Inside them follows the rules of the brain, outside them follows the rules of the spinal cord, and the beans themselves probably follow the brain.

phrases.aramaic: פּוֹלִין יֵשׁ מוּנָּחִין עַל פִּי הַקְּדֵרָה,
phrases.english: There are beans lying at the opening of the pot,
phrases.notes: The 'pot' here means the skull. The 'beans' are little bumps right where the spinal cord leaves the head.

phrases.english: from the beans inward, it is like the inside,
phrases.notes: 'The inside' is the brain, where any hole in the membrane was already said to make it a טריפה.

phrases.english: from the beans outward, it is like the outside,
and the beans themselves, I do not know.
And it stands to reason that they are like the inside.

steps.triggerLanguage: פּוֹלִין יֵשׁ מוּנָּחִין עַל פִּי הַקְּדֵרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion (before this section) about where the brain ends and the spinal cord begins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Inward from the beans counts as the brain and outward counts as the spinal cord. The beans themselves are uncertain but most likely count as the brain.

steps.title: Rabbi Yirmeya finds the beans in a bird
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה examined a bird and found something like two beans at the opening of its skull.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה examined a bird and found something that looked like two beans lying at the opening of its skull.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story. רבי ירמיה checked a bird and saw the same bean-shaped bumps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows the landmark from the previous step is something you can actually see. It is not only found in animals but in birds too. So the same border can be used when checking a bird.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya examined a bird,
and found something like two beans
lying at the opening of the skull.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms from a real examination that the beans landmark exists, in birds as well.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bean-shaped landmark is also found in birds.

steps.title: Which chamber of the heart does the משנה mean?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a heart pierced 'into its chamber' is a טריפה. רבי זירא asks whether this means the small chamber or the large chamber.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'If the heart was pierced into its chamber.' רבי זירא asked: Does that mean the small chamber or the large chamber?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It quotes the משנה about a hole in the heart, and רבי זירא asks which of the heart's chambers it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heart has more than one chamber, and the משנה just says 'its chamber' without saying which. If only one chamber counts, a hole reaching the other one would not make the animal a טריפה. That is why the question matters.

keyTerms.meaning: Asks a question that needs resolving

phrases.english: If the heart was pierced into its chamber,
Rabbi Zeira asked:
Into the small chamber
or into the large chamber?

steps.triggerLanguage: נִיקַּב הַלֵּב לְבֵית חֲלָלוֹ, בָּעֵי רַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, moving from the brain to the heart.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'its chamber' in the משנה means the small chamber or the large chamber of the heart.

steps.title: אביי answers from the lung ruling
steps.stepSummary: אביי points to the lung. רב explained רבי שמעון's words 'into the bronchial tubes' to mean the large bronchial tube, so the heart should also mean the large chamber.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Why are you unsure? Didn't we learn in the משנה that רבי שמעון says the lung is not a טריפה unless it is pierced into the bronchial tubes? And רבה בר תחליפא said, quoting רבי ירמיה בר אבא in the name of רב, that this means it must be pierced into the large bronchial tube.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רבי זירא by comparing the heart to a similar ruling about the lung.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the lung, רב said the hole must reach the big main tube, not just any small tube. אביי reasons that the heart works the same way, so 'its chamber' should mean the large chamber.

keyTerms.meaning: Why are you unsure? (the answer is already known)
Isn't it so that...? (introduces a source the listener should know)
The bronchial tubes in the lung

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
What is your question?
Didn't we learn in the Mishnah:
Rabbi Shimon says:
"Not unless it is pierced into the bronchial tubes,"
phrases.notes: This is about the lung. רבי שמעון holds a hole only makes it a טריפה once it reaches the tubes.

phrases.english: and Rabba bar Tachlifa said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba said that Rav said:
Not unless it is pierced into the large bronchial tube.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: מַאי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ? מִי לָא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's question by comparing the heart to the lung.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The heart means the large chamber, just as רבי שמעון's lung ruling means the large bronchial tube according to רב.
steps.raayaObject: That 'its chamber' means the large chamber.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון in the משנה about the lung, as explained by רב.

steps.title: The comparison fails because the wording is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects אביי's comparison. The lung משנה uses the plural 'tubes', which points to the main tube they all pour into. The heart משנה just says 'its chamber', which could mean either one.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? There, the משנה says 'into the bronchial tubes', meaning the place where all the tubes pour into. But here it says 'into its chamber'. What difference is there between a large chamber and a small chamber?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on אביי. It says the lung and the heart cannot be compared, because the wording of the two משניות is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the lung, the plural 'tubes' hints at one main tube that collects all the others, so the word itself points to the large one. In the heart, the משנה just says 'chamber' with no hint, and both chambers fit that word equally well. So אביי's proof does not work, and רבי זירא's question is still open.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare these? (rejects a comparison)
What difference is it to me? (both options are the same)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'what difference is it to me' as the final ruling that both chambers count. Here it only means the word 'chamber' does not point to either one, so אביי's proof fails.

phrases.english: How can you compare these?
There it teaches "into the bronchial tubes,"
meaning the place into which all the tubes pour,
but here it teaches "into its chamber",
what difference is it to me whether it is a large chamber
or a small chamber!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי הַשְׁתָּא? הָתָם לְבֵית הַסִּמְפּוֹנוֹת קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's proof from the lung.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison between the heart and the lung, so אביי's answer falls.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The lung משנה's plural wording points to the main tube, but the heart משנה's plain word 'chamber' fits either chamber equally.

steps.title: רב and שמואל argue about a hole in the heart's tube
steps.stepSummary: רב says any hole in the קנה הלב makes the animal a טריפה. שמואל says it has to be a hole in most of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the tube of the heart: רב says even a tiny hole makes the animal a טריפה. שמואל says only a hole through most of it does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic, the main tube coming out of the heart, and brings a מחלוקת about how big a hole makes the animal a טריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב treats the tube like the heart itself, where any hole is a problem. שמואל treats it more leniently and needs most of it to be damaged. The rest of this section builds on this argument.

keyTerms.meaning: The tube of the heart, the main artery coming out of the heart
With any amount, even a tiny bit
An animal with a fatal defect, which may not be eaten

phrases.english: The tube of the heart,
Rav says: with any amount,
and Shmuel says: with its majority.

steps.triggerLanguage: קְנֵה הַלֵּב, רַב אָמַר: בְּמַשֶּׁהוּ, וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: בְּרוּבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of the heart's chambers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: any hole in the קנה הלב makes the animal a טריפה. שמואל: only a hole in most of it does.

steps.title: Which tube is the heart's tube?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which blood vessel is called the קנה הלב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which one is the tube of the heart?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask which body part רב and שמואל were talking about. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before we can apply the argument, we need to know which tube in the chest it is about. This is a question about defining the case, not a challenge.

phrases.english: Which one is the tube of the heart?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of the body part in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact identity of the קנה הלב.

steps.title: רב: it is the one in the fat on the sides
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר יצחק quotes רב: the קנה הלב is the tube found in the fat on the sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר יצחק said in the name of רב: it is the one in the fat that sits on the sides.
steps.whatsHappening: רב's answer is given: the heart tube is the one covered in fat 'on the sides'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer points to a tube wrapped in fat. But the word 'sides' is unclear, and the next step questions what it means.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Yitzchak said that Rav said:
The fat that is on the sides.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר רַב: חֵלֶב שֶׁעַל גַּבֵּי דְּפָנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The קנה הלב is the tube in the fat on the sides.

steps.title: Can 'sides' really mean the animal's sides?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: 'sides' can't mean the animal's ribs, since those are not near the heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: Could you really think it means the sides of the animal?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of רב's answer. The animal's sides are far from the heart, so the answer can't mean those.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read plainly, 'sides' sounds like the ribs, which makes no sense for a tube coming out of the heart. This sets up a corrected reading in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Would it enter your mind? A way of saying 'that can't be right'

phrases.english: Sides, could that enter your mind?
phrases.notes: He means the sides of the animal, its ribs, which aren't next to the heart.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the answer in step 8.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The animal's sides, its ribs, are not next to the heart, so the heart tube can't be described as being on them.

steps.title: It means the sides of the lung
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the reading: the tube is the one in the fat on the sides of the lung.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means the one that is on the sides of the lung.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the reading of רב's words. 'Sides' means the sides of the lung, not the sides of the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heart tube runs past the lung, wrapped in fat, so this reading fits. Now we know exactly which tube רב and שמואל argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; brings in a corrected reading

phrases.english: Rather: the one that is on the sides of the lung.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9 by rereading רב's words.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Sides' sounded like the animal's sides, its ribs.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Sides' means the sides of the lung, where the heart tube runs wrapped in fat.
steps.whatToRemember: The קנה הלב is the fatty tube coming out of the heart that runs along the sides of the lung.

steps.title: אמימר: three tubes, each treated like its organ
steps.stepSummary: אמימר, quoting רב נחמן, says there are three tubes: to the heart, the lung and the liver. The lung tube follows the lung's rule, the liver tube follows the liver's rule, and the heart tube is the one in the מחלוקת.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said in the name of רב נחמן: There are three tubes. One branches off to the heart, one to the lung and one to the liver. The lung's tube is treated like the lung. The liver's tube is treated like the liver. About the heart's tube, רב and שמואל argue.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר places the heart tube next to two similar tubes and gives a rule for each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lung tube gets the lung's rule, so any hole makes the animal a טריפה. The liver tube gets the liver's rule, so it is only a problem if it is completely missing. The heart tube is the one רב and שמואל disagree about, which ties back to step 6.

phrases.english: Ameimar said in the name of Rav Nachman:
There are three tubes,
one branches off to the heart,
and one branches off to the lung,
and one branches off to the liver.
The lung's is like the lung,
the liver's is like the liver,
phrases.notes: The liver is only a problem if it is completely gone, so the same goes for its tube.

phrases.english: the heart's, they argue about it.
phrases.notes: 'They' means רב and שמואל from the start of this section.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַמֵּימָר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן: תְּלָתָא קְנֵי הָווּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the discussion from the heart tube to all three tubes in the chest.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lung tube follows the lung's rule, the liver tube follows the liver's rule, and the heart tube is under the מחלוקת of רב and שמואל.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Like the lung' and 'like the liver' don't mean the same rule. Any hole is a problem for the lung, but the liver is only a problem if it is completely missing.

steps.title: מר בר חייא teaches the lung and liver tubes the opposite way
steps.stepSummary: מר בר חייא swaps the rules: the lung tube is like the liver, and the liver tube is like the lung. He agrees that רב and שמואל argue about the heart tube.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר חייא teaches it the other way around: the lung's tube is treated like the liver, and the liver's tube is treated like the lung. About the heart's tube, they argue.
steps.whatsHappening: A second version of אמימר's teaching is given, with the rules for the lung and liver tubes switched.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the lung tube is only a problem if it is completely missing, while any hole in the liver tube makes the animal a טריפה. Both versions agree that the heart tube is the subject of the argument between רב and שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: The opposite, the other way around

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions agree that the heart tube is the one רב and שמואל argue about. They only disagree about which rule goes with the lung tube and which goes with the liver tube.

phrases.english: Mar bar Chiyya teaches it the opposite way:
the lung's is like the liver,
the liver's is like the lung,
the heart's, they argue about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a reversed version of אמימר's teaching in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lung tube follows the liver's rule, the liver tube follows the lung's rule, and the heart tube is under the מחלוקת of רב and שמואל.

steps.title: שמואל rejects רב's ruling on the heart tube
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר יוסף reports רב's ruling about the heart tube to שמואל, and שמואל says that if רב really said this, he knows nothing about טריפות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר יוסף went and told רב's teaching to שמואל. שמואל said to him: If אבא (רב) really said that, then he knows nothing at all about טריפות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story that closes the topic of the heart tube. שמואל hears רב's strict ruling and rejects it very strongly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 11-12 said that רב and שמואל argue about the heart tube. רב's teaching here is the strict view, that any hole in it makes the animal a טריפה. שמואל's sharp words show how firmly he disagrees with that strict view.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching or ruling that a sage said
Injuries or defects that make an animal forbidden to eat, even after proper שחיטה

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the argument about the heart tube was a deep and serious disagreement between רב and שמואל, not a small detail.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Yosef went
and said Rav's teaching in front of Shmuel.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי הָכִי אָמַר אַבָּא –
phrases.english: He (Shmuel) said to him: If Abba said this,
phrases.notes: אבא is רב's own name. שמואל is calling him by it here.

phrases.english: he knows nothing at all about tereifos.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲזַל רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף אַמְרַהּ לִשְׁמַעְתָּא דְרַב קַמֵּיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the topic of the heart tube that steps 11-12 said רב and שמואל argue about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל strongly rejects רב's strict ruling on the heart tube.

steps.title: Broken spine: how badly must the spinal cord be damaged
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a broken spine and brings a ברייתא: רבי says the spinal cord must be cut in its majority, while רבי יעקב says even a hole is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'If the spine was broken.' The Rabbis taught: If the spinal cord was cut in its majority, the animal is a טריפה. These are the words of רבי. רבי יעקב says: Even if it was only pierced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: the line in the משנה about a broken spine. It brings a ברייתא with two opinions about how much damage to the spinal cord makes the animal a טריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי needs a cut through most of the spinal cord. רבי יעקב is stricter: even a small hole makes the animal a טריפה. This is a new subject, separate from the heart tube.

keyTerms.meaning: The spinal cord, the 'string' that runs inside the spine

steps.confusionAlert: Here רבי means רבי יהודה הנשיא, and he is the lenient side (a majority is needed). Don't mix him up with רבי יעקב, who is the strict side.

phrases.english: "The spine was broken"
phrases.notes: These are words quoted from the משנה. Some versions have the word in round brackets, and the word in square brackets is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A spinal cord that was cut through most of it (is a tereifa).
These are the words of Rabbi.
Rabbi Yaakov says: Even if it was only pierced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the heart tube to the next case in the משנה, a broken spine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי: a טריפה only if most of the spinal cord is cut. רבי יעקב: a טריפה even if it is only pierced.

steps.title: רבי ruled like רבי יעקב, but רב הונא says the הלכה is not like him
steps.stepSummary: רבי himself gave a practical ruling like רבי יעקב, yet רב הונא says the הלכה does not follow רבי יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ruled like רבי יעקב. רב הונא said: The הלכה is not like רבי יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us what happened in practice: רבי actually ruled like רבי יעקב's strict view. Then רב הונא gives the final ruling: the הלכה is not like רבי יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is surprising that רבי ruled against his own opinion and followed the stricter view of רבי יעקב. רב הונא decides that, in the end, a hole alone is not enough, so we follow the view that most of the cord must be cut.

keyTerms.meaning: The final law does not follow this opinion

steps.whatToRemember: In practice, a small hole in the spinal cord does not make the animal a טריפה. Most of it has to be cut (רב הונא).

phrases.english: Rabbi ruled like Rabbi Yaakov.
Rav Huna said:
The halacha is not like Rabbi Yaakov.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical outcome of the argument in the ברייתא from step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even though רבי ruled like רבי יעקב, the הלכה does not follow רבי יעקב.

steps.title: How much counts as 'most' of the spinal cord
steps.stepSummary: Since the הלכה needs most of the spinal cord to be cut, the גמרא asks what 'most' is measured by.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is 'most of it'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question to set up the next step: what exactly do we measure when we say 'most' of the spinal cord?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that the rule depends on רבי's 'majority', we need to know what part of the cord is measured. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And how much is 'most of it'?

phrases.english: And how much is "most of it"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact meaning of 'majority' in רבי's opinion, which is the הלכה according to step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What part of the spinal cord the 'majority' is measured by.

steps.title: Two versions of רב's answer: most of the covering, or most of the inner cord
steps.stepSummary: רב says 'most' means most of the outer covering (עור) of the spinal cord. Another version says he meant most of the inner soft cord (מוח).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: Most of its skin (its outer covering). And some say: Most of its brain (the soft cord inside).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with רב's view, but it reports two versions of what רב said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, we look at the outer covering: if most of it is cut, the animal is a טריפה. In the second version, we look at the soft inner cord: if most of that is cut, it is a טריפה even if the covering is whole.

keyTerms.meaning: Its 'skin', meaning the outer covering around the spinal cord
Its 'brain', meaning the soft cord tissue inside

steps.confusionAlert: Both versions belong to רב. They are two reports of what he said, not two different sages arguing.

phrases.english: Rav said: Most of its skin,
phrases.notes: 'Skin' here means the covering that wraps around the spinal cord, not the animal's outer skin.

phrases.english: and some say: Most of its brain.
phrases.notes: 'Brain' means the soft tissue inside the spinal cord.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר: רוֹב עוֹרוֹ, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ: רוֹב מוֹחוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב: the majority is measured by the outer covering. Another version: by the soft inner cord.

steps.title: What if most of the inner cord is cut but the covering is whole?
steps.stepSummary: According to the view that most of the מוח must be cut, a cut in most of the עור is surely enough. But according to the view that most of the עור is needed, what is the law if only most of the מוח is cut?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says 'most of the inner cord,' all the more so most of the covering. According to the one who says 'most of the covering,' what is the law about most of the inner cord?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא works out the two versions of רב from Step 17 and asks an open question about one of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even a cut in the inner מוח is enough to make the animal טריפה, then a cut in the outer covering is clearly enough too (כל שכן). But if the rule is about the covering, we don't know yet whether a cut in most of the inner cord alone also counts. The next step answers this with רב הונא's statement.

keyTerms.meaning: Most of its outer covering (the membrane around the spinal cord)
Most of its inner soft cord

phrases.english: The one who says most of its inner cord
all the more so most of its covering.
According to the one who says most of its covering,
what about most of its inner cord?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר רוֹב עוֹרוֹ – רוֹב מוֹחוֹ מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the two versions of רב's answer and asks about a case the covering-version leaves open.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: According to the covering-view, does a cut in most of the inner cord alone make the animal טריפה?

steps.title: רב הונא: only the covering counts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רב הונא's statement (reported by ניולי) that the 'majority' means most of the covering, and the inner cord makes no difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: ניולי said in the name of רב הונא: The 'majority' that they spoke of is most of the covering; this inner cord neither adds nor takes away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 18 with a statement from רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא says the measure is only the covering. The phrase 'it neither raises nor lowers' means the inner cord has no effect at all: if the covering is mostly whole, a cut in the inner cord does not make the animal טריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: Neither raises nor lowers; makes no difference

phrases.english: Come and hear:
For ניולי said that רב הונא said:
The majority that they said is most of its covering;

phrases.aramaic: מוֹחַ זֶה – לֹא מַעֲלֶה וְלֹא מוֹרִיד.
phrases.english: this inner cord neither raises nor lowers.
phrases.notes: Literally 'neither raises nor lowers'; it just means the inner cord doesn't change the ruling either way.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר נִיוְלִי אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A cut in the inner cord alone does not matter; only the covering counts.

steps.title: A story: רב tells his student not to check the inner cord
steps.stepSummary: רב נתן בר אבין checked the covering and then also checked the inner cord. רב told him that if most of the covering is whole, the inner cord makes no difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נתן בר אבין was sitting before רב. He checked most of the covering, and then was checking most of the inner cord. רב said to him: If most of the covering is whole, this inner cord neither adds nor takes away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life story that supports the same rule as רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The student thought he also had to check the inner cord. רב himself stopped him, showing in practice that once the covering is mostly whole, the animal is fine no matter what the inner cord looks like.

keyTerms.meaning: Was sitting before him (learning from his teacher)

steps.whatToRemember: For the spinal cord, the 'majority' is measured by the outer covering (עור). If most of the covering is whole, a cut in the inner cord (מוח) does not make the animal טריפה.

phrases.english: רב נתן בר אבין
was sitting before רב.
He checked most of its covering,
and was also checking most of its inner cord.
רב said to him:
If most of its covering is intact,

phrases.aramaic: מוֹחַ זֶה אֵינוֹ מַעֲלֶה וְאֵינוֹ מוֹרִיד.
phrases.english: this inner cord neither raises nor lowers.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נָתָן בַּר אָבִין הֲוָה יָתֵיב קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a practical story that backs up רב הונא's rule.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that only the covering counts and the inner cord makes no difference.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's own instruction to רב נתן בר אבין during an actual inspection.

steps.title: A liquid or softened spinal cord makes the animal unfit
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה reports in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי that a spinal cord that became liquid (נתמרך) or soft (נתמסמס) makes the animal פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: If it became liquid, it is unfit. If it became soft, it is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new rule: damage to the spinal cord isn't only a cut. If it turned liquid or mushy, the animal is also פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we spoke about a cut. Now we learn about a different kind of damage, where the cord's texture breaks down. Both a fully liquid cord and a merely soft cord make the animal טריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: Unfit (here, a טריפה that may not be eaten)

phrases.english: רבה בר בר חנה said
that רבי יהושע בן לוי said:
If it became liquid, it is unfit;
if it became soft, it is unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from a cut spinal cord to a spinal cord whose texture was damaged.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A spinal cord that became liquid or soft makes the animal פסול.

steps.title: What exactly is 'liquid' and what is 'soft'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for definitions of the two terms רבי יהושע בן לוי used.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'liquefying' and what is 'softening'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the two words mean, setting up the definitions in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two words sound similar, so we need to know where the line is between them and how bad the damage must be for each one.

phrases.english: What is 'liquefying,'
and what is 'softening'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to define the two terms in the ruling of Step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact meaning of המרכה and המסמסה.

steps.title: Liquid pours like from a jug; soft can't stand up
steps.stepSummary: המרכה is when the cord pours out like water from a jug. המסמסה is when it cannot stand up on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: Liquefying is any case where it pours out like from a jug. Softening is any case where it cannot stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a clear test for each of the two terms.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liquid is the worse case: the cord flows out like water. Soft is a milder case: it still holds together but sags and cannot stand up by itself. Even this milder case makes the animal פסול.
steps.whatToRemember: A spinal cord that turned liquid (pours like from a jug) or soft (can't stand on its own) makes the animal פסול, even without a cut.

phrases.english: Liquefying is any that pours out like from a jug;
softening
phrases.notes: Some versions spell it like the round brackets, and the square brackets have the corrected spelling. It means the same either way.

phrases.english: is any that cannot stand up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the definitional question of Step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: המרכה means it pours like from a jug; המסמסה means it cannot stand on its own.

steps.title: A cord that cannot stand because it is heavy
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks about a spinal cord that cannot stand up because of its weight, not because it is soft.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked: If the cord cannot stand because it is heavy, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה asks about a new case that sits between the definitions just given. The cord cannot stand up straight, but the reason is that it is heavy, not that it went soft.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 23, המסמסה was defined as a cord that 'cannot stand on its own.' רבי ירמיה wants to know whether the test is only the result (it does not stand) or also the reason (softness). If the cord is heavy but firm, does it still count as המסמסה?

keyTerms.meaning: Asks a real question that needs an answer

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked:
If it cannot stand because of its heaviness,
what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the edge of the definition of המסמסה given in step 23
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a cord that cannot stand because of weight, not softness, counts as נתמסמס and makes the animal פסול

steps.title: The question is left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cannot answer רבי ירמיה's question, so it stays open (תיקו).
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the question stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says it has no answer to רבי ירמיה's question, so the question stays open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means no proof was found either way. The case of a heavy cord stays a doubt, and the גמרא moves on.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question remains unresolved

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רבי ירמיה's question without an answer
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The status of a cord that cannot stand because of its weight remains an unresolved doubt.

steps.title: Softened is unfit, emptied is kosher
steps.stepSummary: בי רב rule that a softened cord (נתמסמס) makes the animal פסול, but an emptied cord (נתמזמז) is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רב says: If the cord softened, the animal is unfit. If it was emptied, the animal is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling separates two kinds of damage. A cord that went soft makes the animal unfit, but a cord whose inner tissue drained out leaves the animal kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two Hebrew words sound almost the same, but בי רב give them opposite results. נתמסמס is softening caused by disease, which is serious. נתמזמז is some tissue draining away, which they consider harmless.

keyTerms.meaning: Was emptied: some tissue drained out of the cord

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up נתמסמס (with a ס) and נתמזמז (with a ז). They sound alike but have opposite rulings here.

phrases.english: The school of Rav says:
if it softened, it is unfit;
if it was emptied, it is kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new distinction between softening and emptying
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Softening (נתמסמס) makes the animal פסול; emptying (נתמזמז) leaves it כשר.

steps.title: A ברייתא says emptied is טרפה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says an animal whose tissue was emptied (נתמזמז) is טרפה, which goes against בי רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says an animal whose nerve tissue was emptied is טרפה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ruling of בי רב with a ברייתא that seems to say the exact opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בי רב said נתמזמז is kosher. Here רבי שמעון בן אלעזר uses that very word and says טרפה. A teaching from the time of the ברייתא carries more weight, so this is a strong challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat
The soft nerve tissue (here, inside the cord)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
an animal whose nerve tissue was emptied is a tereifa!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of בי רב
steps.kashyaTarget: בי רב's ruling that נתמזמז is כשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא uses the same word, נתמזמז, and rules the animal טרפה.

steps.title: The ברייתא really said 'softened'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the correct wording of the ברייתא is נתמסמס, not נתמזמז.
steps.simpleTranslation: That teaching actually said 'softened.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by fixing the wording of the ברייתא. It really says 'softened,' not 'emptied.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the ברייתא reads נתמסמס, it says the same thing as בי רב: softening makes the animal טרפה. So there is no contradiction, and emptying stays kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: In that teaching, the word said was 'softened'

phrases.english: In that one, 'softened' was stated.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is saying the right wording of the ברייתא has the ס word, so it matches בי רב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Corrects the wording of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא says emptying (נתמזמז) is טרפה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא says softening (נתמסמס) is טרפה, which agrees with בי רב.

steps.title: לוי's comment suggests emptying is deadly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again from a story: לוי saw a man hit his head and said his tissue was 'emptied,' which seems to mean the man would not live.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But לוי was sitting in a bathhouse and saw a man who banged his head. לוי said: This man's tissue has been emptied. Doesn't that mean he will not live?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether emptying is really harmless. It brings a story where לוי used the word נתמזמז about an injured man, and that seems to mean the man would die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If emptying is fatal for a person, it should also make an animal a טרפה, since טרפה means a defect the animal cannot survive. That would go against בי רב's ruling that נתמזמז is כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that really so? (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: Is that so?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא לֵוִי הֲוָה יָתֵיב בֵּי מַסּוּתָא,
phrases.english: But Levi was sitting in a bathhouse,
he saw a certain man
who banged his head,
and he said: This one's nerve tissue has been emptied.
Does it not mean that he will not live?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי, וְהָא לֵוִי הֲוָה יָתֵיב בֵּי מַסּוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to בי רב, after the first one was answered
steps.kashyaTarget: בי רב's ruling that נתמזמז is כשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: לוי used נתמזמז to describe an injury that seems fatal, so emptying should make an animal טרפה.

steps.title: לוי meant the man would not have children
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that לוי meant the man would become unable to have children, not that he would die.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: No. לוי meant that the man would not be able to have children.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by explaining לוי's words differently. לוי was talking about the man's ability to have children, not about whether he would live.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal is טרפה only if the damage is fatal. Losing the ability to have children is not fatal, so לוי's comment does not show that emptying is fatal, and בי רב's ruling stands.
steps.whatToRemember: Softening (נתמסמס) makes the animal טרפה. Emptying (נתמזמז) does not, because it is not fatal. At most it affects having children.

phrases.english: Abaye said: No;
he meant to say that he will not have children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the story of לוי
steps.terutzHavaAmina: לוי meant the man would die.
steps.terutzMaskana: לוי meant the man would not be able to have children, which is not fatal, so emptying stays כשר.

steps.title: How far down does the spinal cord go?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the spinal cord ends, since only damage to the cord itself makes an animal טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until where does the spinal cord extend?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question: where the spinal cord counts as ending. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting the spinal cord makes an animal טרפה. Below a certain point, though, the strand no longer counts as the spinal cord. The גמרא wants to know where that line is.

phrases.english: Until where does the spinal cord extend?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the length of the spinal cord
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The lower end of the spinal cord for the laws of טרפה

steps.title: Until 'between the branches'
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל says the spinal cord extends until 'between the branches.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: Until between the branches.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers that the spinal cord counts until the spot called בין הפרשות, 'between the branches.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'branches' are where the cord splits into strands near the back legs. A cut above that point makes the animal טרפה. The next story shows that this spot was hard to point out on a real animal, so it ends up being taught in words.

keyTerms.meaning: Between the branches: where the cord splits near the thighs

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Until between the branches.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of how far down the cord goes
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The spinal cord extends until בין הפרשות, where it branches out.

steps.title: רב דימי asks to be shown the spot
steps.stepSummary: Before traveling to בי חוזאי, רב דימי בר יצחק asks רבי יהודה to show him where 'between the branches' is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי בר יצחק wanted to go to בי חוזאי. He came to רבי יהודה and said: Master, show me where 'between the branches' is.
steps.whatsHappening: A story begins. רב דימי בר יצחק is about to travel and wants to be shown exactly where the spot שמואל described is located.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hearing the words 'between the branches' was not enough. He needed to see the spot itself so he could rule correctly on his own where he was going.

keyTerms.meaning: A distant place (the region of Khuzistan)

phrases.english: Rav Dimi bar Yitzchak

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה קָא בָּעֵי לְמֵיזַל לְבֵי חוֹזָאֵי,
phrases.english: wanted to go to Bei Chozai.
He came before Rabbi Yehuda
and said to him:
Let the master show me
where 'between the branches' is.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב דִּימִי בַּר יִצְחָק הֲוָה קָא בָּעֵי לְמֵיזַל לְבֵי חוֹזָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story asking to see the spot שמואל described
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact physical location of בין הפרשות

steps.title: A fat kid and a thin kid both fail
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה asks for a young goat to demonstrate on. The fat one hides the spot in fat, and the thin one has bones sticking out, so neither works.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Go bring me a young goat and I will show you. He brought a fat goat. רבי יהודה said: The spot is buried too deep and cannot be seen. He brought a thin goat. רבי יהודה said: The bones stick out too much and the spot cannot be seen.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה starts to answer by showing the spot on a real animal. The first two goats are not suitable, so the demonstration is not finished yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fat covers the spot, and bones on a thin animal hide it. The story shows how hard it is to find the spot, and it continues after this point.

keyTerms.meaning: They are buried too deep (in the fat)
They stick out too much (the bones)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: זִיל אַיְיתִי לִי גְּדִי
phrases.english: He said to him: Go bring me a young goat
and I will show you.
He brought him a fat young goat.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בְּלִיעָן טְפֵי וְלָא יְדִיעַ.
phrases.english: He said to him: They are buried too deep, and it cannot be recognized.
He brought him a thin one.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בְּלִיטָן טְפֵי וְלָא יְדִיעַ.
phrases.english: He said to him: They stick out too much, and it cannot be recognized.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: זִיל אַיְיתִי לִי גְּדִי וְאַחְוִי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering רב דימי's request through a demonstration that is still in progress
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No final answer yet. Fat and thin goats are both unsuitable for showing the spot, and the story continues.

steps.title: רבי יהודה teaches שמואל's tradition about the branches in words
steps.stepSummary: Instead of showing the spot on an animal, רבי יהודה quotes שמואל. A cut until the first branch makes the animal a טרפה. A cut at the third is כשר. For the second, שמואל does not know the הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Come, I will teach you a tradition. This is what שמואל said: until the first branch, the animal is a טרפה. At the third, it is כשר. At the second, I do not know.
steps.whatsHappening: The goats did not work for showing the spot, so רבי יהודה answers רב דימי's request with a teaching in words, quoting שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back in step 32, 'between the branches' was too vague. Now שמואל's tradition splits the area into three branching points. Before the first branch, a cut is still on the real spinal cord, so the animal is a טרפה. After the third branch, the cord no longer counts, so the animal is כשר. The second point stays an open question.

keyTerms.meaning: A received tradition, a teaching passed down from a teacher (not the name of the Talmud here)
An animal with a fatal defect, which may not be eaten
I do not know, an honest admission that the הלכה is unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: Cut before the first branch makes it a טרפה. Cut at the third branch is כשר. The second branch is a doubt that שמואל left unresolved.
steps.confusionAlert: Here the word גמרא does not mean 'the Talmud.' It means a tradition received from one's teacher.
steps.whyThisMatters: שמואל openly says 'I do not know' about the middle point. That leaves a real doubt in הלכה about a cut in that area.

phrases.english: He said to him: Come, I will teach you a tradition,
This is what Shmuel said:
Until the first [branch], it is a tereifa,
The third, it is kosher,
The second, I do not know.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The demonstration in step 34 failed, so this step finishes the answer to רב דימי's request in words.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Exactly where 'between the branches' is, the point where the spinal cord ends for טרפה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Before the first branch the animal is a טרפה, at the third it is כשר, and the second is unresolved.

steps.title: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע opens a question
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע begins to ask a question. The content of the question comes in the next part of the text.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע asked:
steps.whatsHappening: This line only sets up the next move. It tells us that רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע is about to ask a question, but the question itself comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בעי signals a real question that has no clear answer yet, not an attack. It most likely builds on שמואל's three-branch tradition that was just taught. The details come next.

keyTerms.meaning: Asks a question, raises a real doubt that needs an answer

phrases.aramaic: בָּעֵי רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, asks:
